guide.title: Rexxar's Overview
guide.text:
Rexxar is a Bruiser followed by
his bear companion, named Misha, who fights alongside him and offers him support in
various ways throughout the game. Compared to most other Heroes, playing Rexxar is
a unique experience since you have to control both him and Misha at the same
time.

guide.title: Rexxar's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Hard to gank if played properly
Misha can hold Capture Points for Objectives
Good crowd control
Weaknesses
No mobility
Not a real Hero when Misha is dead
Mana management can be crucial to win the solo lane sometimes

guide.title: Rexxar's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Rexxar synergizes with
Rexxar pairs very well with Heroes who add additional
crowd control to combine with
Misha, Charge! in no particular order
(such as Johanna that can group enemy Heroes for you
or Malfurion that can make your engage last longer).
Mages will easily benefit from the
additional crowd control provided by Misha, Charge! and
by Unleash the Boars to a lesser extent (like
Jaina that deals way more damage if her target is standing still or
it is being Slowed down more than she can do on her own).
Rexxar is countered by
When laning, Rexxar is weak against Heroes who have a gap-closer to
reach Rexxar behind Misha, damage to pressure Misha to death or kill Rexxar, and
self-sustain to make good trades.
In team fights, Rexxar suffers from Heroes who can dive
him and dodge his crowd control thanks to their high
mobility (such as Zeratul).

guide.title: Rexxar's Maps
guide.text:
Rexxar's stronger maps
Rexxar's average maps
Rexxar's weaker maps
Rexxar excels on Braxis Holdout and Dragon Shire
because he can get a lot of value from having 2 bodies: Rexxar can
safely take care of Minions while Misha stays on the Capture Point
of the Objective.
Rexxar does well on Tomb of the Spider Queen because
he can safely collect Gems with Misha and he cannot lose Gems
when only Misha dies.

guide.title: Rexxar's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Spirit Swoop can be used to Slow enemy Heroes, making it easier to hit them with Basic Attacks and Misha, Charge!.
Misha, Charge! is great for peeling. Use [Alt + W] to cast Misha, Charge! towards Rexxar without having to aim with your mouse cursor.
Mend Pet costs a lot of Mana, so you should avoid using it when Misha is almost full Health and a Regeneration Globe is enough for healing her.
Bestial Wrath is more effective when enemy Heroes cannot easily disengage or when there is a valuable Objective or Capture Point to contest.
Unleash the Boars can be used to Slow enemy Heroes, making it easier to hit them with Basic Attacks and Misha, Charge!.
Misha, Focus! allows you to move Misha around. Use [Alt + D] to self-cast Misha, Focus! and quickly call Misha to your side without having to aim with your mouse cursor.
Misha can be an excellent tool to intercept skillshot Abilities that were originally aimed at Rexxar or a vulnerable allied Hero nearby.
Misha always spawn behind Rexxar. You can use this to your advantage by quickly turning away as soon as she is about to spawn, to have her spawn closer to enemy Heroes and/or block a skillshot Ability.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Rexxar's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Rexxar is currently one of the best Offlaners in
the game when it comes to contesting a Capture Point because
Misha be on it while Rexxar safely takes care of enemy Minions.
Misha's strong crowd control makes
Rexxar a valuable asset during team fights as well, both for
engaging and for peeling,
unless Misha is dead.
Rexxar requires good micro management in order to unfold his maximum potential
and, as such, he sometimes can feel quite overwhelming to newer players. Controlling
Misha feels challenging at first, however, once the initial learning curve
has been overcome, Rexxar's strong chasing and kiting capabilities and the ability
to Stun multiple foes at the same time make him a force to be reckoned with.

abilities.title: Rexxar's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
Spirit Swoop can be used to Slow enemy Heroes, making it easier to hit them with Basic Attacks and Misha, Charge!.
Misha, Charge! is great for peeling. Use [Alt + W] to cast Misha, Charge! towards Rexxar without having to aim with your mouse cursor.
Mend Pet costs a lot of Mana, so you should avoid using it when Misha is almost full Health and a Regeneration Globe is enough for healing her.
Bestial Wrath is more effective when enemy Heroes cannot easily disengage or when there is a valuable Objective or Capture Point to contest.
Unleash the Boars can be used to Slow enemy Heroes, making it easier to hit them with Basic Attacks and Misha, Charge!.
Misha, Focus! allows you to move Misha around. Use [Alt + D] to self-cast Misha, Focus! and quickly call Misha to your side without having to aim with your mouse cursor.
Misha can be an excellent tool to intercept skillshot Abilities that were originally aimed at Rexxar or a vulnerable allied Hero nearby.
Misha always spawn behind Rexxar. You can use this to your advantage by quickly turning away as soon as she is about to spawn, to have her spawn closer to enemy Heroes and/or block a skillshot Ability.

abilities.title: Spirit Swoop
abilities.text:
Spirit Swoop
(Q)
Rexxar
Mana: 40
Cooldown: 7 seconds
Deal 141 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in a line, slowing them by 30% for 2 seconds.
Spirit Swoop is a solid and straightforward Ability that enables Rexxar to
Slow multiple enemies in order to hunt them more efficiently,
but you usually want to hit a single Hero because trying to hit more will
force you to go out of position and risk dying for nothing.

abilities.title: Misha, Charge!
abilities.text:
Misha, Charge!
(W)
Rexxar
Mana: 45
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Misha charges in a line, dealing 150 (+4% per level) damage and stunning enemies for 1.25 seconds.
Misha, Charge! is by far the most impactful Ability when playing as Rexxar.
If you manage to control and position Misha effectively, this
Ability allows you to Stun and damage multiple enemies at the same time, which
can single handedly decide the outcome of a team fight.
What we find
particularly strong is the fact Misha can leap behind enemy Heroes and
potentially body block them in narrow
choke points. Furthermore, it
can be used defensively as well if you need Misha to retreat away from the
enemy or intercept skillshots that were aimed at Rexxar
or his allies.

abilities.title: Mend Pet
abilities.text:
Mend Pet
(E)
Rexxar
Mana: 70
Cooldown: 10 seconds
Heal Misha for 714 (+4% per level) Health over 5 seconds.
Being able to heal Misha is incredibly beneficial to Rexxar's
overall combat performance because he feels fairly weak without Misha. Mend Pet
has a relatively low cooldown, which means you can heal Misha at
least once or twice during an average team fight, but pay attention to your Mana
because it consumes a considerable amount of that.
Since this Ability provides a
heal-over-time instead of a burst heal, you will have to use it proactively in
order to keep Misha alive. It is worth mentioning that Misha will respawn nearby
Rexxar after a short while (around 5-10 seconds during the early-mid game and
20-30 seconds during the late game) if she is killed in battle.

abilities.title: Bestial Wrath
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Bestial Wrath
(R)
Rexxar
Heroic
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 50 seconds
Increases Misha's Basic Attack damage by 200% for 12 seconds.
Bestial Wrath causes
Misha's Basic Attacks to hit very hard, something that can be used to
pressure priority targets in the enemy backline.
All that said, smart opponents will
just focus down Misha and render this strategy useless.
In that case, use Misha to attack the enemy frontline instead.

abilities.title: Unleash the Boars
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Unleash the Boars
(R)
Rexxar
Heroic
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Release a herd of boars that track down all enemy Heroes in a direction, dealing 110 (+4% per level) damage, revealing, and slowing enemies by 40% for 5 seconds.
Unleash the Boars is a strong
Slow that will help your team to engage,
to hunt down fleeing enemies, and to reveal nearby
Stealthed Heroes. Do not underestimate the Slow provided
because it will help your team to position and move better than the enemy team
during a team fight.

abilities.title: Misha, Focus!
abilities.text:
Misha, Focus!
(D)
Rexxar
Cooldown: 0.125 seconds
Passive: Misha gains 15% move speed.
Command Misha to attack a specific enemy or move to a point and wait.
Targeting Rexxar commands Misha to retreat to his position, gaining 30% move speed until she reaches Rexxar.
Targeting Misha commands her to hold her current position.
Misha, Focus! is Rexxar's ability to control Misha very precisely, for instance
if you want her to keep attacking a specific enemy target, regardless of what
Rexxar attacks. Furthermore, it allows Rexxar to use Misha as a
designated scouting tool by placing her in key locations to provide vision to
the rest of the team. It is worth mentioning that when clicking on Rexxar himself, Misha gains a slight
Movement Speed buff, which can oftentimes be crucial to guarantee her survival.
Using Misha, Focus! does not dismount or break channels.
You can use this at your advantage to reposition Misha and mess with enemy Heroes while
Rexxar is channeling an Objective (such as a Tribute on Cursed Hollow)
or using Hearthstone. When you need to join your team, you can also start mounting
while Rexxar is clearing the last couple of Minions and/or catching Experience Globes.
Rexxar and Misha share the cooldown and effect of Healing Fountains. Misha can be sent
to the Healing Fountain instead of Rexxar by using Misha, Focus! on it.
Rexxar and Misha do not share the effect of Regeneration Globes, so they both need to be
in range if you want both of them to regenerate Health and/or Mana. Quests that require
Regeneration Globes have their progress shared between Rexxar and Misha.
Misha is a separate entity from Rexxar. When killed, Misha respawns after 14 seconds plus 0.5 seconds per Team Level.
When Rexxar is alive, killing Misha rewards 1 Takedown credit and 0.25 Hero Kills worth of Experience.
When Misha is dead, killing Rexxar rewards 1 Takedown credit and 0.75 Hero Kills worth of Experience.
When Misha is alive, killing Rexxar automatically kills Misha and therefore rewards 2 Takedown credits
and 1 Hero Kill worth of Experience. Misha always respawns together with Rexxar if they are both dead.

talent_pages.title: Level 1 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
✔
Bird of Prey
(Level 1)
Rexxar
Increases Spirit Swoop's damage by 150% to Minions.
Bird of Prey is a strong Talent that increases
Rexxar's damage against Minions when hitting them with Spirit Swoop.
The waveclear provided by this Talent
has high value for Rexxar when being played as Offlaner.
?
Easy Prey
(Level 1)
Rexxar
Increases Misha's basic attack damage to Minions and Mercenaries by 150%, and Misha gains 50 Armor against Minions and Mercenaries, reducing damage taken by 50%.
Easy Prey is a decent Talent that increases
Misha's damage and Armor against both Minions and Mercenaries.
In theory this is a useful Talent because it allows
you to clear Mercenary Camps all by yourself. In practice Mercenary Camps should be
captured by the rest of the team because the Offlaner
should soak as much Experience as possible during the
early game and also because there is always a chance
that the enemy team tries to invade the Mercenary Camp that you are working on.
If you want to play this Talent anyway because you do not expect your team to take care of Mercenary Camps,
feel free to pick it but only go for Mercenary Camps if there are no enemy Minions in your lane, if Misha
can capture it while you are soaking because the Mercenary Camp is really close to
the lane, or ask for an allied Hero to cover your lane while you are away.
?
Flare
(Level 1)
Rexxar
Cooldown: 20 seconds
Fire a flare at an area, revealing it for 20 seconds.
Flare is a situational Talent that has some use
when the enemy team has a dangerous
ganker Hero, however, you can generally play safer
without having to spend a Talent for it.
Use it on cooldown
around the most dangerous zone of your lane and completely deny any enemy attempt
to surprise you. This trick is particularly effective against Heroes
with Stealth (for example Nova).
Due to its low cooldown, it can also be cast to give vision in
bushes, which helps your teammates avoid
dangerous facechecking, or around corners
of impassable terrain.

talent_pages.title: Level 4 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
?
Hungry Bear
(Level 4)
Rexxar
Misha's Basic Attacks heal her for 4.5% of her maximum Health.
Hungry Bear is a situational Talent
that improves Misha's self-sustain
without costing Mana. This is quite helpful in the early game.
You should only pick this Talent when playing against a Hero that can
easily consume Block charges
on a Map where early game is important
(notably Braxis Holdout).
✔
Hunter-Gatherer
(Level 4)
Rexxar
Quest: Gathering a Regeneration Globe increases Rexxar and Misha's Health Regeneration by 1 per second, up to 25 per second.
Reward: After gathering 25 Globes, Rexxar and Misha gain 15 Armor.
Hunter-Gatherer is a solid all-round Talent that gives
Armor to both Rexxar and Misha, a recommended choice to increase Rexxar's
survivability in late-game team fights.
?
Grizzled Fortitude
(Level 4)
Rexxar
Every 6 seconds, Rexxar and Misha gain 75 Physical Armor against the next enemy Hero Basic Attack, reducing the damage taken by 75%.
Stores up to 2 charges. Both Rexxar and Misha have their own charges.
Grizzled Fortitude is a situational Talent that periodically gives both Rexxar and Misha
Physical Armor in the form of
Block charges.
Block charges are especially valuable
when facing Heroes with slow but heavy-hitting Basic Attacks (such as Hanzo) and
terrible when playing against Heroes with fast-hitting Basic Attacks (D.Va,
Genji, Kharazim, Lúcio, Tassadar, Tracer,
and Tychus). Heroes with Clones (for example Nova) can consume them faster
too, however, it is generally not a problem because their AI will not always target you.
✘
Animal Husbandry
(Level 4)
Rexxar
Rexxar and Misha gain 2 Maximum Health every second Rexxar remains alive. These bonuses are lost on Rexxar's death.
Animal Husbandry is a high-risk high-reward choice
that should be avoided. Thanks to his time-based scaling, Rexxar and Misha can
gain more Health for the late game as long as Rexxar
manages to survive (similar to Devil's Due on Diablo).
To make this Talent less risky, it is crucial to be aware of potential
ganks at any give time. Furthermore,
defensive Talents like Feign Death at Level 16 or
Hardened Skin
at Level 20 can help Rexxar to stay alive and keep stacking Animal Husbandry.
Avoid picking this Talent because it can easily become a
dead Talent in the late game.

talent_pages.title: Level 7 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
?
Crippling Talons
(Level 7)
Rexxar
Increases Spirit Swoop's slow amount to 50% and its duration to 3.5 seconds.
Crippling Talons is a good Talent that empowers
the Slow provided by Spirit Swoop
and increases its duration as well.
We find this Talent particularly useful when the enemy team can easily get rid of Misha,
a move that will force you to play without Misha-related Talents (like Aspect of the Beast).
?
Taking Flight
(Level 7)
Rexxar
Increases Spirit Swoop's range by 20%. If Spirit Swoop hits an enemy Hero, the Mana cost is refunded and its cooldown is reduced by 2 seconds.
Taking Flight is a situational Talent that can
be picked when you need poke damage in order to
win the offlane against some Heroes
(Leoric comes to mind).
The cooldown reduction, albeit not that high, can be useful to slightly increase
the waveclear provided by Bird of Prey at Level 1
and/or the uptime of Aspect of the Hawk at Level 13.
✔
Aspect of the Beast
(Level 7)
Rexxar
Misha's Basic Attacks lower the cooldown of Misha, Charge! by 1 second.
Aspect of the Beast is a strong Talent that
allows you to cast Misha, Charge! more often if Misha is allowed
to stick on enemy Heroes and to execute multiple Basic Attacks on them.
We find the additional crowd control provided by this Talent
great during team fights as it can be used for doing multiple things, defensively and/or offensively.
Pick this Talent when you want more tools to interrupt enemy Abilities,
more crowd control, or more peeling.

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
?
Bestial Wrath
(Level 10)
Rexxar
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 50 seconds
Increases Misha's Basic Attack damage by 200% for 12 seconds.
Bestial Wrath is a decent Heroic Ability that empowers
Misha's Basic Attacks, something that can be used to
add more damage on the focused enemy Hero.
Go for this
Talent only when you need more damage to win the offlane
on Maps where that is important (such as Braxis Holdout) or when
your team does not have enough damage to secure kills because of a bad draft.
✔
Unleash the Boars
(Level 10)
Rexxar
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Release a herd of boars that track down all enemy Heroes in a direction, dealing 110 (+4% per level) damage, revealing, and slowing enemies by 40% for 5 seconds.
Unleash the Boars is a strong Heroic Ability which provides a powerful
Slow that will help your team to engage,
to hunt down fleeing enemies, and to reveal nearby
Stealthed Heroes.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
✔
Aspect of the Hawk
(Level 13)
Rexxar
When Spirit Swoop hits an enemy Hero, Rexxar gains 125% Attack Speed for 4 seconds. Misha's Basic Attacks increase the duration of this buff by 0.75 seconds.
Aspect of the Hawk is a strong Talent that
provides Rexxar with a significant amount of Attack Speed, which increases
his overall combat performance quite a bit.
By empowering his Attack Speed, this Talent turns Rexxar in a
threat for enemy Heroes within range. Be careful when using it
because you may easily become a target for the enemy team.
If you have no way to escape, then use it to retaliate.
Note that this Talent also works when Misha is dead,
so it is a good choice when playing against team compositions
that can easily get rid of Misha before or during team fights.
?
Dire Beast
(Level 13)
Rexxar
Rexxar and Misha's Basic Attacks increase the damage of the next Misha, Charge! by 15%, stacking up to a 150% bonus.
Dire Beast can inflict great burst damage, which is
why we recommend picking this Talent. Remember that you can stack it on Minions before a team fight
happens so that Misha will not need to stack it on enemy Heroes, a trick that
can occasionally make the difference between a won or lost team fight.
?
Wildfire Bear
(Level 13)
Rexxar
Misha deals 28 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies.
Wildfire Bear is a small damage boost for clearing
Minions and killing Heroes, something that is not really worth spending a Talent on.
Besides that, it is capable of revealing invisible enemies and untargetable objects
(for example
Creep Tumor by Zagara)
on the battlefield as soon as Misha gets near them.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
?
Thrill of the Hunt
(Level 16)
Rexxar
Rexxar's Basic Attacks increase both his and Misha's Movement Speed by 25% for 2 seconds.
Thrill of the Hunt's bonus Movement Speed works incredibly
well with
Misha's ability to Stun retreating targets, while it also allows Rexxar
to escape more easily himself.
?
Primal Intimidation
(Level 16)
Rexxar
Activate to Slow the Attack Speed by 50% and Movement Speed by 20% of Heroes and Summons near Rexxar and Misha for 2.5 seconds.
Passive: Heroes and Summons that attack Rexxar or Misha have their Attack Speed slowed by 20% for 2.5 seconds.
Primal Intimidation offers a good amount of
protection against enemy Heroes that rely on Basic Attacks as their primary
damage source (such as Raynor), but you rarely want this Talent over
Feign Death.
✔
Feign Death
(Level 16)
Rexxar
Cooldown: 35 seconds
Rexxar fakes his death, becoming Invulnerable and untargetable for 5 seconds. During this time you control Misha.
Feign Death
puts Rexxar in Stasis, which makes it an ideal tool to
dodge enemy Abilities. It is good to know
that Rexxar can still control Misha while
this Talent is active.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Rexxar
talent_pages.text:
✘
Spirit Bond
(Level 20)
Rexxar
Increases the duration of Bestial Wrath by 50% and Misha's Basic Attacks heal Rexxar for 50% of her damage dealt during Bestial Wrath.
Spirit Bond fails to have a major impact during team
fights. While increased duration on Bestial Wrath is
quite useful, the life steal is barely noticeable because Misha will not be able
to attack a lot at this stage of the game, especially if team fights are short.
✔
Kill Command
(Level 20)
Rexxar
Unleash the Boars deals 50% more damage and Roots for 1.5 seconds.
Kill Command is always a great Talent because the
Root
effect makes for an efficient tool to initiate team fights, something that is
extremely valuable in the late game.
?
Frenzy of Kalimdor
(Level 20)
Rexxar
Rexxar's Basic Attacks deal 10% more damage, and Misha's Basic Attacks slow the target by 20% for 1.25 seconds.
Frenzy of Kalimdor provides a Slow
effect and a damage boost. It is your preferred choice for when you take
Bestial Wrath at Level 10.
Another good strategy is to pick this Talent instead of Kill Command
when your team decides to go for the Core to end the game and Unleash the Boars
is on cooldown because it increases your damage per second on the Core.
?
Hardened Skin
(Level 20)
Rexxar
Cooldown: 60 seconds
Rexxar and Misha gain 75 Armor for 4 seconds, reducing damage taken by 75%.
Hardened Skin adds a lot of Armor
to Rexxar and Misha, but it is not advised to waste this Tier for a
defensive Talent—unless the enemy team is just bursting
you down to win each and every team fight—because the Root
provided by Kill Command
is just too strong to pass, the damage and utility provided by
Frenzy of Kalimdor is more useful as well,
and you probably have Feign Death to stay alive.
